caption:
Austin is adding $10 million to help eligible homeowners repair their homes.

On October 8, the Austin Housing Finance Corporation approved amendments for its G.O. Repair! program, extending six nonprofit partners’ contracts through September 30, 2028. The additional funding raises the combined contract ceiling to $32 million.

The program supports repairs for eligible low-income homeowners within Austin city limits. Partner Austin Habitat for Humanity lists roofing, electrical, plumbing, heating and cooling, and accessibility improvements among the types of work its home-repair program can address.

Why it matters locally: Keeping existing homes safe and usable is part of preserving Austin’s housing supply. Owners struggling with essential repairs may have an assistance option worth checking.

Eligibility, approved work and timing depend on the provider’s screening and available funding. Habitat’s online interest form places homeowners on an inquiry waitlist; it is not an approved repair application.

Sources: Austin Housing Finance Corporation, October 8, 2026; Austin Habitat for Humanity’s current home-repair guidance.
